- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to reflect bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to reflect bearish momentum.  
- Model consistently underestimates sharp upward moves (e.g., spikes above 75–80) — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for such spikes.  
- Model overestimates downward moves (e.g., drops below 65–68) — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for such drops.  
- Forecast shows gradual, flat trend but true outcome has strong mean reversion — reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid over-optimism.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 2–5 days — adjust forecast to start rising earlier if sentiment is positive or falling earlier if sentiment is negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small positive spikes (e.g., 0.20), model tends to ignore them — amplify small sentiment-driven corrections.  
- If model forecast is flat or trending slowly but true outcome shows volatility, reduce forecast smoothness — allow ±1–2% deviation from trend for volatile periods.
